_comment: Confidential ACI container group for aci_session_master (this
directory's own Dockerfile) -- one h2 attested-session per launch,
then the process exits and Azure tears the group down. Shape copied
from Microsoft's own real tutorial template
(container-instances-tutorial-deploy-confidential-containers-cce-arm,
raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/confidential-container-demos/
main/hello-world/ACI/arm-template.json) -- the `sku`/
`confidentialComputeProperties` pair is what turns an ordinary
container group into a confidential one; without them the group
deploys but nothing in it validates.
`image` defaults to a placeholder -- resolve-image-digest.sh fills in
the real `ghcr.io/directionallyai/aci-worker/aci-session-worker@sha256:...`
reference by digest (never a mutable tag: the CCE policy's own `id`
field pins the same digest, so a tag that moved out from under it
would just make az confcom's policy generation and this template
disagree about which image runs, not any kind of real substitution
attack -- the SNP report's `layers` check is what actually gets
verified at container start).
`ccePolicy` starts empty -- `az confcom acipolicygen -a arm-template.json`
fills it in (and prints its own SHA-256, the value
update-policy-hashes.sh/agent.py's AZURE_ACI_EXPECTED_POLICY_HASH
needs) once `image` above is a real, resolved digest.
restartPolicy is hardcoded to Never, not a parameter -- see
aci_session_master.rs's own module doc comment for why `Always`/
`OnFailure` would silently turn 'run one session and exit' into an
unbounded restart loop reusing the same container. Not something a
caller of this template should be able to override.
Public IP, not a private VNET endpoint -- deliberate for now, not an
oversight: the h2 attested-session protocol already assumes a
hostile network between client and container (that's the whole point
of the handshake), so the trust boundary here is attestation, not
network reachability. Worth revisiting if there's ever a reason to
hide the container's existence entirely, not because a public IP
weakens what's actually being verified.

metadata.description: Location for all resources -- must be a region where the ACI Confidential SKU is available.

Container image to deploy, pinned by digest -- resolve-image-digest.sh's own output. Never a mutable tag: the CCE policy generated against this template bakes this exact digest into its own `id`/`layers` fields.
Matches AZURE_ACI_PORT's own default in aci_session_master.rs -- the single TCP port the h2 attested-session client connects to.
One session, one -e/repl call -- not a long-lived service under sustained load.
The number of CPU cores to allocate to the container.

AZURE_ACI_MAA_ENDPOINT -- e.g. sharedeus2.eus2.attest.azure.net. No default: get_maa_token() refuses to run against an unpinned MAA instance the same way agent.py's own AZURE_ACI_MAA_EXPECTED_ISSUER does on the verifying side.
AZURE_ACI_ACCEPT_TIMEOUT_SECS -- how long the container waits for its one client connection before exiting.
AZURE_ACI_WORKER_TIMEOUT_SECS -- how long worker.py gets to finish running the submitted -e/repl code.
